claims.text: The initial high-entropy alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
Mechanical loading is the intervention associated with the proposed degradation.
Nano-scale precipitates form in the alloy.
Nano-scale precipitates act as stress concentrators.
Stress concentration at the precipitates promotes crack initiation.
Stress concentration at the precipitates promotes crack propagation.
Precipitate-mediated crack initiation and propagation cause a loss of toughness or brittle fracture during mechanical loading.
The proposed behavior applies under demanding service involving high temperatures, high stresses, and corrosive environments.
The stated service boundary is temperature below 800°C.
The stated service boundary is stress below 1000 MPa.
The stated service boundary is corrosion rate below 10^-4 mm/year.
A controlled comparison between otherwise comparable alloys with and without nano-scale precipitates can test the proposed mechanism.
Toughness, fracture toughness, and microstructure are the proposed experimental observables.
Similar toughness in precipitate-free and precipitate-containing material would falsify a detrimental precipitate effect.
Improved toughness in the precipitate-free material relative to the precipitate-containing material would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says precipitates reduce toughness, so improved toughness in the precipitate-free alloy relative to the precipitate-containing alloy would support, not falsify, the proposed detrimental precipitate mechanism. Only equivalent behavior would undermine the claimed precipitate effect.
